concepts.title: StoreKit APIs for commitment-based subscription billing plans
concepts.canonicalSummary: A group of StoreKit additions that let an app read and select pricing for subscription products sold under a billing plan that pairs monthly payments with a twelve-month commitment, and merchandise that plan through built-in SwiftUI subscription styles.

citations.locator: StoreKit > New Features (all four items, radar 150388310, 150388542, 150388746, 150389069)
citations.supports: That these four related additions form one reusable capability area rather than four unrelated features.

concepts.title: App receipt reports a literal null app version
concepts.canonicalSummary: A defect in which the field carrying the application's version inside the encoded app receipt is populated with the four-character text null rather than the real version string, so receipt validation reads a meaningless value.

citations.locator: StoreKit > Resolved Issues > first item (radar 171614522, FB22114908)
citations.supports: The existence and shape of the receipt version defect that this concept names.

concepts.title: Current entitlements come back empty under a non-Gregorian system calendar
concepts.canonicalSummary: A defect in which a customer holding a live subscription is reported as having no current entitlements while their device runs a calendar system other than Gregorian, so a paying subscriber can be denied access to paid content.

citations.locator: StoreKit > Resolved Issues > second item (radar 173415174)
citations.supports: The defect's trigger condition and its effect on subscriber entitlement lookups.

concepts.title: StoreKit testing does not pick up subscription price edits
concepts.canonicalSummary: A defect in the in-Xcode StoreKit testing environment in which edits to a subscription's price are not observed by the testing harness, so a developer cannot exercise price-change behaviour locally.
aliases: StoreKit Testing in Xcode price observation

citations.locator: StoreKit Testing in Xcode > Known Issues > only item (radar 175848494, FB22647785)
citations.supports: The defect's scope and its status as an open issue at the time of the document.

concepts.title: Test session ignores the selected store configuration when unit tests run
concepts.canonicalSummary: A defect in which the store test session object fails to adopt whichever store configuration the developer picked while unit tests execute, so those test actions fail.

citations.locator: StoreKitTest > Resolved Issues > only item (radar 172583218, FB22237318)
citations.supports: The defect's trigger and its effect on unit test runs.

concepts.title: Test session fails to reach the test environment on Simulator
concepts.canonicalSummary: A defect in which StoreKit test sessions do not establish a working connection to the store test environment while running under Simulator, so test actions that depend on that connection fail.

citations.locator: StoreKit > Resolved Issues > only item (radar 174738526, FB22500243)
citations.supports: The defect's Simulator-specific trigger, distinguishing it from the separately numbered configuration-selection defect resolved in visionOS 26.5.

concepts.title: Missing authorization prompt for blood pressure data types
concepts.canonicalSummary: A defect in which the permission screen an app relies on does not appear when the app asks for access to either of the two blood pressure quantity types, leaving the request unresolvable by the person using the device.

citations.locator: HealthKit > Resolved Issues > first item (radar 177652061)
citations.supports: The two data types affected and the nature of the failure.

concepts.title: Time-weighted averages inflated by overlapping samples
concepts.canonicalSummary: A defect in which statistics queries that weight discrete health quantities by time produce values that are too high when the underlying samples cover overlapping periods, with resting heart rate among the affected metrics.

citations.locator: HealthKit > Resolved Issues > second item (radar 178157672)
citations.supports: The query type affected, the direction of the error, and the sample condition that triggers it.

concepts.title: Spotlight index groundwork for the next major release

citations.locator: visionOS 26.6 section > first sentence
citations.supports: That Apple itself describes this release as reshaping the Spotlight index ahead of the next generation.

disagreements.topic: Whether Apple's Developer Releases feed can serve as the identity source for the visionOS pre-release seeds in this cycle.

positions.position: Apple's Releases feed retains a per-entry record for only three of the twelve assigned appearances: the visionOS 26.5 public release, the visionOS 26.6 first beta, and the visionOS 26.6 public release. For the nine other assigned dates the feed's entry-identifier space is either wholly empty or holds only entries for other platforms.
MacRumors reports a visionOS seed on each of those nine dates, in a continuous and internally consistent series that names each seed's position in its cycle.

AppleInsider independently reports a visionOS seed on each of the same nine dates and additionally publishes a build identifier and the identifier it replaced, forming an unbroken chain across both cycles.

disagreements.recommendedBoundary: Treat the feed's silence as non-retention rather than non-occurrence. The build chains reported by AppleInsider are internally consistent and terminate on identifiers Apple itself published, which is strong circumstantial support for the intervening seeds. Identity for those nine appearances should rest on the two independent newsrooms, and the production citations that point at Apple Developer for those dates should be corrected because they cannot be resolved to any Apple page describing the seed.

positions.position: MacRumors titles its 2026-07-20 article around release candidates and describes the seeds as the final versions barring late defects, which labels the appearance a release candidate.

AppleInsider's article for the same date is internally inconsistent: its retained HTML title element calls the seeds sixth developer betas while its on-page headline and body call them release candidates. Its build list gives the visionOS identifier as the same one Apple later shipped.

disagreements.recommendedBoundary: The appearance is best classified as a release candidate: both publishers' body text says so, and the build identifier matches the shipping release. The assignment's stable event identifiers for visionOS 26.6 run m0 to m4 and then m6, leaving m5 unaccounted, which is consistent with production already holding this appearance under m5. qualityChecks.reviewNotes: Independent evidence review by evidence-reviewer-visionos26-c, performed without reliance on the researcher's self-report. Status set to returned for one material defect. THE DEFECT: claim-v265-public-security-scale and the summary of v265-public-occurrence-security-catalogue both describe the visionOS 26.5 security catalogue as spanning system areas 'including the kernel, WebKit, WebRTC, image and audio handling, Spotlight, Siri, Mail and Notes'. In the retained evidence (source-004.selected.txt) the visionOS 26.5 component entry list runs from Accelerate at line 281 to WebRTC at line 713, and 'Additional recognition' begins at line 735. Siri, Mail and Notes appear only at lines 785, 773 and 781, inside Additional recognition, which is Apple's researcher-acknowledgement list ('We would like to acknowledge X for their assistance') and not a list of documented fixes carrying vulnerability identifiers. No Siri, Mail or Notes component entry exists in the catalogue. The claim therefore contradicts its own locator, which explicitly bounds the list 'above the Additional recognition section'. Left as-is for the researcher to correct: remove Siri, Mail and Notes from both strings, or restate them as acknowledgements rather than fixed components. The kernel, WebKit, WebRTC, ImageIO/AppleJPEG, Audio and Spotlight portions of the same sentence are correct. This is material because the target is recommended fullArticle and the occurrence is labelled documented/confirmed at high confidence, so the error would publish as vendor-documented fact. The parallel visionOS 26.6 sentence (claim-v266-public-security-scale) was checked the same way and is correct: App Store, Contacts, CoreMedia, Game Center, ImageIO, Kernel, MediaRemote, WebKit, WebKit Canvas, WebKit Storage and Wi-Fi all sit inside the component list above Additional recognition at line 1101. WHAT WAS VERIFIED CLEAN: exact target closure, all 12 assignment target IDs present in assignment order with all 14 identity fields matching field-by-field; all local IDs unique across 36 sources, 11 concepts, 61 claims, 21 occurrences, 28 gaps and 3 disagreements, with no cross-collisions; all 222 citation references resolve to declared sources and every citation carries a locator and a supports note; source-023 is the only uncited source and its non-use is explained on the source record and used only for the batch chronology note; all 72 evidence files re-hashed with both node crypto and shasum -a 256 and re-measured with wc -c, with zero mismatches against rawSha256, selectedTextSha256, rawBytes and selectedTextBytes; the negative-probe artifact also re-hashes to the value quoted on source-010. Locators were resolved against retained text well beyond the required sample, covering the release-notes heading inventories and tracking numbers in source-001 and source-002, the reproducible counts in source-004 (40 'Available for' lines, 48 distinct CVEs) and source-005 (84 and 99), the security index rows in source-006, the three Apple Releases entries in source-007, source-008 and source-009, the feed inventory in source-010, and all eleven visionOS build rows in source-024 through source-035, whose supersession chain is unbroken and matches every build claim exactly. Evidence states are correct: all 11 confirmed occurrences rest on firstPartyDocumentation; both corroborated occurrences have two genuinely independent newsrooms; the 8 reported occurrences each rest on one bylined article that directly states the fact and each declines to re-assert the harder public-beta claim. Inheritance is correct: delta is used only three times, twice for security catalogues carrying an explicit Released line matching the appearance date and once for the visionOS 26.6 Spotlight statement in Apple's per-version consumer document, which was checked against the neighbouring visionOS 26.5 section to confirm it is not boilerplate; the cumulative labelling of release-note items is right because source-001 and source-002 carry no date, no build and no per-seed section and so cannot localize an item within a cycle. Build discipline is correct: exactly three identifiers are confirmed (23O471, 23O5728e, 23O770), each backed by an Apple-published Releases entry, and the other nine are reported off a single publisher and excluded from build documents. Source independence is handled honestly: source-006 and source-010 are marked non-independent as indexes over the same lineage, and source-016 and source-022 are flagged as restating Apple for release content while independent for date and installation procedure. Copyright was re-checked independently rather than trusted: 485 reader-facing strings were tested for five-consecutive-word normalized overlap against all 73 retained evidence files (108,555 distinct 5-grams). 100 runs reach five tokens and none reaches six; every one is a version string split by the tokenizer, a document title, a URL, an Apple heading name, or a match against the researcher's own extraction notes. The verbatim publisher article bodies and the verbatim Apple security documents produced zero hits, and there are zero non-null shortQuote fields anywhere in the packet. Commit hygiene is clean: tmp/research-evidence/ is gitignored at .gitignore line 59, the batch evidence directory appears in neither git status nor the index, and the committed files contain no cookie, token, credential or private contact data. No production write occurred: no sanity exec, --apply, publish or deploy string appears anywhere in the packet, and no file outside research-handoffs/apple-visionos-26-c/ and tmp/research-evidence/apple-visionos-26-c/ was touched in the batch window. The outcome distribution of 2 complete, 1 partial and 9 noSubstantiveNotesFound is honest rather than lazy: the negative findings are backed by a reproducible per-date walk of Apple's Releases entry-identifier space, retained at tmp/research-evidence/apple-visionos-26-c/negative-probe-developer-releases-feed.selected.txt, whose per-date results match every negative finding exactly, including the differentiated cases where 2026-05-04 holds one iOS entry and 2026-06-29 holds three other-platform entries, and including the correctly distinguished visionOS 26.6 Beta 1, which does have an Apple entry and is therefore given a nonMaterial rather than material citation gap. NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS for the researcher, none of which gate the packet: source-029 independently reports the App Store monthly-payment-with-twelve-month-commitment subscription option and could be added as a second, independent citation on v265-public-occurrence-commitment-billing-apis; the eight inherited developer-only-track occurrences cite only the MacRumors article for their date even though the matching AppleInsider article for the same date independently reports a developer seed and would support the same fact; and the researcher's copyright check was scoped to 33 publisher-authored captures whereas this review indexed all 73 retained files, with the same clean result. RE-REVIEW SCOPE: once the two strings on the visionOS 26.5 public target are corrected, no other gate needs re-running; every other check above was verified against retained evidence and is unaffected by that edit.
